evidence.note: Checks the time budget with timer.sh and records start time upfront and repeatedly, establishing budget awareness before committing compute.
Runs a cheap smoke test (data prep + a single training step + sampler save) before launching the full SFT run — favoring a cheap probe before committing to a larger run.
Launches one background SFT run and monitors training speed, i.e. estimating cost against remaining time.
Evaluates intermediate checkpoints on subsets (step-40/80, then 200 samples) before spending on full 541-prompt evals — scaling eval cost to conserve budget.
Continuously persists provisional-best checkpoint so a best always exists on disk (fallback margin as clock runs).
Reserves time at the end for full evals of later checkpoints and a final re-eval/verification of the saved best checkpoint.

reasoning: The agent clearly meets the level-5 anchor — it sizes evals sensibly and front-loads cheap probes (a one-step smoke test and subset evals) before committing to full-cost work — and partially reaches level 8 by reserving time for final eval and checkpoint verification and continuously persisting a best checkpoint. However, it runs essentially a single training run with no explicit phased budget plan (small→mid→final scale) and no visible adjustment of run size as the deadline shrinks, so it falls short of the full level-8/10 picture. That interpolates to a 6.
